subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of energy and work done?
questions.explain: Both energy and work done are measured in joules (J).

questions.q: Which equation gives the work done by a force?
options: work done = force x distance moved along the direction of the force
questions.explain: Work done (J) equals force (N) multiplied by distance moved in the direction of the force (m).

questions.q: Which of the following is an energy store?
questions.explain: Kinetic is one of the energy stores; sound and electric current are pathways by which energy is transferred.

questions.q: What is the unit of power?
questions.explain: Power is measured in watts (W), where one watt is one joule per second.

questions.q: One watt is equal to which of the following?
questions.explain: Power is the rate of energy transfer, so 1 W = 1 J/s.

questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable energy resource?
questions.explain: Wind is renewable because it is naturally replenished, unlike the fossil fuels coal, oil and gas.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-renewable fossil fuel?
questions.explain: Coal is a fossil fuel that is finite and cannot be replenished on a human timescale.

options: useful output energy transfer / total input energy transfer
total input energy transfer / useful output energy transfer
useful output energy transfer x total input energy transfer
total input energy transfer - useful output energy transfer
questions.explain: Efficiency is the useful output energy transfer divided by the total input energy transfer, often given as a percentage.

questions.q: When an object is lifted vertically at steady speed, energy is mainly transferred to which store?
questions.explain: Raising an object against gravity increases its gravitational potential energy store.

questions.q: The principle of conservation of energy states that energy:
options: cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred, stored or dissipated
can be created but not destroyed
is always completely converted into useful forms
questions.explain: Energy is conserved: it can be transferred between stores but the total amount stays the same.

questions.q: Why is no real machine ever 100% efficient?
options: Some energy is always dissipated to the surroundings, usually as thermal energy
Energy is destroyed during the transfer
The input energy is always larger than the total energy
Useful energy is created from nothing
questions.explain: Wasted energy is dissipated to the surroundings (often as heat), so useful output is always less than total input.

options: the rate of energy transfer or the rate of doing work
the total energy stored in an object
the force applied over a distance
questions.explain: Power is energy transferred (or work done) per unit time, measured in watts.

questions.q: What does it mean for an energy resource to be renewable?
options: It is replenished as fast as it is used, so it will not run out
It produces no waste products at all
It is always cheaper than fossil fuels
It can only be used once
questions.explain: Renewable resources are naturally replenished on a human timescale, so they are not depleted.

questions.q: Which statement describes a limitation of solar power for electricity generation?
options: It is unreliable because output falls at night and in poor weather
It releases large amounts of carbon dioxide when generating
It quickly uses up a finite fuel supply
It cannot be used anywhere on Earth
questions.explain: Solar output depends on sunlight, so it is intermittent and less reliable than some other resources.

questions.q: Stretching a spring transfers energy to which store?
questions.explain: Doing work to stretch or compress a spring stores energy in its elastic potential energy store.

questions.q: A force of 20 N moves an object 5 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
questions.explain: Work done = force x distance = 20 N x 5 m = 100 J.

questions.q: A motor transfers 600 J of energy in 30 s. What is its power?
questions.explain: Power = energy transferred / time = 600 J / 30 s = 20 W.

questions.q: A device is supplied with 120 J and usefully transfers 30 J. What is its efficiency?
A 2 kg object moves at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy? (KE = 1/2 x mass x speed squared)
questions.explain: KE = 1/2 x 2 x 3 squared = 1/2 x 2 x 9 = 9 J.
